```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "docs/images/")
library(lme4)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

# Load Data
if (!requireNamespace("HanPolNet", quietly = TRUE)) {
    # Fallback or install if not present
    devtools::install("local_packages/HanPolNet", upgrade = "never")
}
library(HanPolNet)
library(gt)
data("pollen_deposition", package = "HanPolNet")

# Load Interaction Data for Table S3
interaction_data_Succisa_22_24 <- get_interaction_data(
    years = c(22, 23, 24),
    plant_species = "Suc_pra",
    is_pollinator = TRUE,
    remove_zeros = TRUE,
    standardize = FALSE
)

# Prepare data for VCA (Inter-Annual Model structure)
model_data <- pollen_deposition %>%
    filter(!is.na(heterospecific_pollen)) %>%
    mutate(
        year_fac = as.factor(year),
        plant_id = inflorescence_id,
        # Calculate Prop HP (avoiding division by zero)
        total_pollen = heterospecific_pollen + conspecific_pollen,
        prop_HP = ifelse(total_pollen > 0, heterospecific_pollen / total_pollen, 0)
    )
```

# Section S1: Variance Partitioning Model Diagnostics

To transform the data for the Variance Component Analysis, we compared three approaches: Raw Counts, Log transformation (`log1p`), and Square-Root transformation (`sqrt`).

Model Structure: `variable ~ 1 + (1 | year_fac / plant_id)`

```{r}
#| label: diagnostics-helper
#| echo: false
#| results: hide
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# Helper function to fit 3 models and plot diagnostics
run_transformation_diagnostics <- function(data, variable_name, title_prefix) {
    # Extract variable
    y <- data[[variable_name]]
    # Handle zeros for Log
    y_log <- log1p(y)
    # Handle distribution for Sqrt
    y_sqrt <- sqrt(y)

    # 1. Fit Models
    # A) Raw
    m_raw <- lmer(y ~ 1 + (1 | year_fac / plant_id), data = data)
    # B) Log
    m_log <- lmer(y_log ~ 1 + (1 | year_fac / plant_id), data = data)
    # C) Sqrt
    m_sqrt <- lmer(y_sqrt ~ 1 + (1 | year_fac / plant_id), data = data)

    # 2. Plotting Helper
    make_plots <- function(model, suffix) {
        df <- data.frame(Fitted = fitted(model), Residuals = resid(model))

        p_hist <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Residuals)) +
            geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.7) +
            labs(title = paste("Hist:", suffix), x = "", y = "Freq") +
            theme_minimal()

        p_res <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Fitted, y = Residuals)) +
            geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
            geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
            labs(title = paste("Res vs Fit:", suffix), x = "Fitted", y = "Res") +
            theme_minimal()
        return(list(p_hist, p_res))
    }

    pl_raw <- make_plots(m_raw, "Raw")
    pl_log <- make_plots(m_log, "Log")
    pl_sqrt <- make_plots(m_sqrt, "Sqrt")

    # Combine
    grid.arrange(
        pl_raw[[1]], pl_log[[1]], pl_sqrt[[1]],
        pl_raw[[2]], pl_log[[2]], pl_sqrt[[2]],
        nrow = 2, ncol = 3,
        top = title_prefix
    )
}
```

## S1.1 Heterospecific Pollen (HP)

```{r}
#| label: diag-hp
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostics for Heterospecific Pollen (HP)."
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 12
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
run_transformation_diagnostics(model_data, "heterospecific_pollen", "Heterospecific Pollen")
```

**Selection**: The raw data (Left) shows severe heteroscedasticity. Both comparisons suggest stabilization, but Square-Root was chosen for alignment with standard count data practices.

## S1.2 Conspecific Pollen (CP)

```{r}
#| label: diag-cp
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostics for Conspecific Pollen (CP)."
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 12
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
run_transformation_diagnostics(model_data, "conspecific_pollen", "Conspecific Pollen")
```

**Selection**: CP loads are generally higher than HP but also exhibit skew. Transformations improve normality. The same Square-Root transformation is applied for consistency.

## S1.3 Proportion HP (HP / Total)

```{r}
#| label: diag-prop
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostics for Proportion HP (HP / (CP+HP))."
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 12
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
run_transformation_diagnostics(model_data, "prop_HP", "Proportion HP")
```

**Selection**: Proportions are bounded \[0,1\]. While Binomial/Beta models are theoretically superior, for the purpose of VCA (partitioning variance), the Square-Root transformation provides a reasonable approximation of normality for the residuals.

# Section S2: Model Selection for CP-HP Relationship

To determine the functional form of the relationship between Conspecific (CP) and Heterospecific (HP) pollen deposition, we compared Linear (Type 1) and Exponential (Type 3) models using Akaike Information Criterion (AIC).

**Data Aggregation**: We aggregated pollen counts to the plant level (mean per plant) to account for multiple stigmas sampled from the same individual.

**Model Selection Criteria**: If the Exponential model provided a significantly better fit (\$\Delta \> 2) compared to the Linear model, it was selected. Otherwise, the simpler Linear model was preferred.

```{r}
#| label: model-diagnostics-selection
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostic plots for the selected models (Linear or Exponential) for each year. Comparisons based on AIC."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-width: 10
library(gridExtra)

# 1. Prepare Aggregated Data (Same as MS)
model_selection_data <- pollen_deposition %>%
    mutate(plant_id = paste(year, inflorescence_id, day, sep = "_")) %>%
    group_by(year, plant_id) %>%
    summarise(
        mean_HP = mean(heterospecific_pollen, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean_CP = mean(conspecific_pollen, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(is.finite(mean_HP) & is.finite(mean_CP))

# Helper function to get diagnostics for the BEST model of a year
get_year_diagnostics <- function(yr) {
    dat <- subset(model_selection_data, year == yr)

    # Fit Linear
    m_lin <- lm(mean_HP ~ mean_CP, data = dat)
    aic_lin <- AIC(m_lin)

    # Fit Exponential
    m_exp <- tryCatch(
        nls(mean_HP ~ a * exp(b * mean_CP),
            data = dat,
            start = list(a = max(dat), b = -0.01)
        ),
        error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (is.null(m_exp)) {
        # Fallback start
        m_exp <- tryCatch(
            nls(mean_HP ~ a * exp(b * mean_CP),
                data = dat,
                start = list(a = mean(dat), b = -0.001)
            ),
            error = function(e) NULL
        )
    }

    aic_exp <- if (!is.null(m_exp)) AIC(m_exp) else Inf

    # Select Best
    if (aic_exp < (aic_lin - 2)) {
        best_model <- m_exp
        type <- "Exponential (Type 3)"
        delta_aic <- aic_lin - aic_exp
        resids <- resid(best_model)
        fitted_vals <- fitted(best_model)
    } else {
        best_model <- m_lin
        type <- "Linear (Type 1)"
        delta_aic <- 0
        resids <- resid(best_model)
        fitted_vals <- fitted(best_model)
    }

    # Diagnostic Plots
    title_res <- paste0(yr, ": ", type, "\nResid vs Fitted")
    title_qq <- paste0(yr, ": Q-Q Plot")

    p_res <- ggplot(data.frame(F = fitted_vals, R = resids), aes(x = F, y = R)) +
        geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
        labs(title = title_res, x = "Fitted", y = "Residuals") +
        theme_minimal()

    p_qq <- ggplot(data.frame(R = resids), aes(sample = R)) +
        stat_qq() +
        stat_qq_line(color = "red") +
        labs(title = title_qq, x = "Theoretical", y = "Sample") +
        theme_minimal()

    return(list(p_res, p_qq))
}

# Generate plots for all 3 years
plots_22 <- get_year_diagnostics(2022)
plots_23 <- get_year_diagnostics(2023)
plots_24 <- get_year_diagnostics(2024)

# Arrange
grid.arrange(
    plots_22[[1]], plots_22[[2]],
    plots_23[[1]], plots_23[[2]],
    plots_24[[1]], plots_24[[2]],
    ncol = 2
)
```

# Section S3: Diagnostic Plots for Slope Comparison Model

To validate the use of the square-root transformation for the "Slope Showdown" analysis (aggregated plant-level data), we examined the residual diagnostics of the linear model.

**Model**: `lm(sqrt(mean_HP) ~ mean_CP * as.factor(year), data = aggregated_data)`

```{r}
#| label: fig-sqrt-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostic plots for the Square-Root Transformed Model. A) Residuals vs Fitted showing no obvious patterns (homoscedasticity). B) Q-Q Plot showing reasonable normality."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10
# Re-create the aggregated data locally for the supplemental plot
model_data_agg <- pollen_deposition %>%
    mutate(plant_id = paste(year, inflorescence_id, day, sep = "_")) %>%
    group_by(year, plant_id) %>%
    summarise(
        mean_HP = mean(heterospecific_pollen, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean_CP = mean(conspecific_pollen, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(is.finite(mean_HP) & is.finite(mean_CP)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(year)) %>%
    mutate(Year = as.factor(year))

# Fit the model used in the main text
fit_sqrt_supp <- lm(sqrt(mean_HP) ~ mean_CP * Year, data = model_data_agg)

# Diagnostic Plots
fig_dir <- file.path("output", "figures")
if (!dir.exists(fig_dir)) dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE)

png(file.path(fig_dir, "fig_sqrt_diagnostics.png"), width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", res = 300)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(fit_sqrt_supp, which = 1, main = "A. Residuals vs Fitted")
plot(fit_sqrt_supp, which = 2, main = "B. Normal Q-Q")
invisible(dev.off())

if (!requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("svglite", repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org")
svglite::svglite(file.path(fig_dir, "fig_sqrt_diagnostics.svg"), width = 10, height = 5)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(fit_sqrt_supp, which = 1, main = "A. Residuals vs Fitted")
plot(fit_sqrt_supp, which = 2, main = "B. Normal Q-Q")
invisible(dev.off())

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(fit_sqrt_supp, which = 1, main = "A. Residuals vs Fitted")
plot(fit_sqrt_supp, which = 2, main = "B. Normal Q-Q")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

<br>

**Table S1. Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and estimated marginal means for pairwise slope contrasts. (A) ANOVA results evaluating the interactive effects of Conspecific TPD and Year on Heterospecific Pollen (HP) accumulation. (B) Pairwise slope contrasts quantifying interannual differences in the rates of HP accumulation across standard-density (2022, 2023) and high-density (2024) years.**

```{r}
#| label: slope-showdown
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(flextable)
library(emmeans)

aov_res <- as.data.frame(anova(fit_sqrt_supp))
aov_table <- data.frame(
    Predictor = gsub("sqrt\\(mean_CP\\)", "Conspecific Pollen (CP)", rownames(aov_res)),
    Df = aov_res$Df,
    Sum_Sq = round(aov_res$`Sum Sq`, 3),
    Mean_Sq = round(aov_res$`Mean Sq`, 3),
    F_value = round(aov_res$`F value`, 2),
    P_value = format.pval(aov_res$`Pr(>F)`, eps = 0.001, digits = 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
aov_table[is.na(aov_table)] <- ""

slopes_em <- emtrends(fit_sqrt_supp, pairwise ~ Year, var = "mean_CP")
contrasts_res <- as.data.frame(slopes_em$contrasts)
contrasts_table <- data.frame(
    Contrast = contrasts_res$contrast,
    Estimate = round(contrasts_res$estimate, 3),
    SE = round(contrasts_res$SE, 3),
    Df = round(contrasts_res$df, 1),
    t_ratio = round(contrasts_res$t.ratio, 2),
    P_value = format.pval(contrasts_res$p.value, eps = 0.001, digits = 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

flextable(aov_table) %>%
    set_header_labels(
        Predictor = "Predictor",
        Df = "df",
        Sum_Sq = "Sum Sq",
        Mean_Sq = "Mean Sq",
        F_value = "F",
        P_value = "p-value"
    ) %>%
    add_header_lines(values = "A) ANOVA Results") %>%
    autofit() %>%
    theme_vanilla()

flextable(contrasts_table) %>%
    set_header_labels(
        Contrast = "Contrast",
        Estimate = "Estimate",
        SE = "SE",
        Df = "df",
        t_ratio = "t-ratio",
        P_value = "p-value"
    ) %>%
    add_header_lines(values = "B) Pairwise Slope Contrasts") %>%
    autofit() %>%
    theme_vanilla()
```

# Section S4: Overview of Pollen Load Sampled Individuals

The following table provides an overview of all individually sampled pollinators for the pollen load analysis.

<br>

**Table S2**: Overview of Pollen Load Sampled Individuals (2024)  
*Number of sampled individuals per pollinator species and collection date.*

```{r}
#| label: table-s2-pollen-load-individuals
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(gt)

# Ensure pollen load data is loaded
pollen_load_data <- read.csv("data/pollen_load_and_guts_2024_Succisa_pratensis.csv")
pollen_load_clean <- pollen_load_data %>%
    mutate(
        year = as.numeric(year),
        morphogroup = case_when(
            grepl("Eristalis", pollinator_species) ~ "Eristalis spp.",
            grepl("Bombus", pollinator_species) ~ "Bombus spp.",
            pollinator_species %in% c("Apis_mellifera", "Apis mellifera") ~ "Apis mellifera",
            grepl("Syrphus", pollinator_species) ~ "Syrphus spp.",
            grepl("Helophilus", pollinator_species) ~ "Helophilus spp.",
            TRUE ~ "Other"
        )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(year))

pollen_load_summary <- pollen_load_clean %>%
    mutate(
        Date = format(as.Date(date, format = "%m/%d/%Y"), "%b %d"),
        Species = gsub("_", " ", pollinator_species)
    ) %>%
    group_by(
        `Pollinator Morphogroup` = morphogroup,
        `Pollinator Species` = Species,
        Date
    ) %>%
    summarise(
        Count = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(
        names_from = Date,
        values_from = Count,
        values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    mutate(Total = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) %>%
    arrange(`Pollinator Morphogroup`, desc(Total))

library(flextable)
flextable(as_grouped_data(pollen_load_summary, groups = "Pollinator Morphogroup")) %>%
    set_header_labels(
        `Pollinator Species` = "Pollinator Species",
        Total = "Total"
    ) %>%
    theme_vanilla() %>%
    set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1) %>%
    italic(j = "Pollinator Species", part = "body") %>%
    fontsize(size = 9, part = "all")
```

# Section S4: Pollinator Community Composition

Table S4 presents the abundance and relative abundance of all pollinator taxa recorded across the three study years. **Note on Abundance**: "Abundance" (Count) represents the raw number of recorded interaction events (unstandardized). Relative abundance (%) is calculated as the species' count divided by the total number of visits for that year.

<br>

**Table S4**: Raw abundance (Count) and relative abundance (%) of all pollinator taxa across study years

```{r}
#| label: table-s3-abundance
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)

# Calculate Counts and Relative (%) Abundance per Year
rel_abund <- interaction_data_Succisa_22_24 %>%
    # Filter out NA or unknown species
    filter(!is.na(pollinator_id) & pollinator_id != "NA") %>%
    group_by(year, pollinator_id) %>%
    summarise(count = sum(interaction_count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    mutate(
        yearly_total = sum(count),
        pct = (count / yearly_total) * 100
    )

# Calculate Grand Total for Sorting
grand_totals <- rel_abund %>%
    group_by(pollinator_id) %>%
    summarise(grand_total = sum(count)) %>%
    arrange(desc(grand_total))

# Reshape for Display
table_s3 <- rel_abund %>%
    # Round for display
    mutate(
        count = as.integer(count),
        pct = round(pct, 2)
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(
        id_cols = pollinator_id,
        names_from = year,
        values_from = c(count, pct),
        values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    # Join grand total to sort
    left_join(grand_totals, by = "pollinator_id") %>%
    arrange(desc(grand_total)) %>%
    select(-grand_total) %>%
    # Reorder columns to be Year-grouped: Count_22, Pct_22, Count_23, Pct_23...
    select(
        Species = pollinator_id,
        `2022 (Count)` = count_22,
        `2022 (%)` = pct_22,
        `2023 (Count)` = count_23,
        `2023 (%)` = pct_23,
        `2024 (Count)` = count_24,
        `2024 (%)` = pct_24
    )

# Print Table
# Print Table
library(flextable)
table_s3 %>%
    flextable() %>%
    set_header_labels(
        Species = "Species",
        `2022 (Count)` = "Count 2022",
        `2022 (%)` = "% 2022",
        `2023 (Count)` = "Count 2023",
        `2023 (%)` = "% 2023",
        `2024 (Count)` = "Count 2024",
        `2024 (%)` = "% 2024"
    ) %>%
    theme_vanilla() %>%
    bg(part = "header", bg = "#F0F0F0") %>%
    bold(part = "header") %>%
    set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1) %>%
    fontsize(size = 9, part = "all")
```

# Section S4: Variance Partitioning Components

The following tables detail the variance components (Inter-Annual and Intra-Annual) for Conspecific (Table S5) and Heterospecific (Table S6) pollen deposition models.

<br>

**Table S5**: Variance partitioning of square-root transformed conspecific TPD  
*Results for Global (Inter-Annual) and 2024 (Intra-Annual) analyses.*

```{r}
#| label: table-s9-s10-vca-components
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(lme4)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1. Prepare data (shared for both)
vca_data_supp <- pollen_deposition %>%
    filter(!is.na(heterospecific_pollen) & !is.na(conspecific_pollen)) %>%
    mutate(
        sqrt_HP = sqrt(heterospecific_pollen),
        sqrt_CP = sqrt(conspecific_pollen),
        year_fac = as.factor(year),
        date_fac = as.factor(paste(year, day, sep = "_")),
        plant_id = inflorescence_id
    )

# 2. General Function for Two-Part VCA (Same logic as main text)
run_twopart_vca_supp <- function(data, variable_col, metric_label) {
    extract_lmer_var <- function(model, name) {
        vc <- VarCorr(model)
        df <- as.data.frame(vc)
        if (!("Residual" %in% df$grp)) {
            sigma_sq <- attr(vc, "sc")^2
            df <- rbind(df, data.frame(grp = "Residual", var1 = NA, var2 = NA, vcov = sigma_sq, sdcor = attr(vc, "sc")))
        }
        total_var <- sum(df$vcov)
        df$percent <- (df$vcov / total_var) * 100
        df$Part <- name
        df$level <- dplyr::case_when(
            grepl("inflorescence", df$grp) ~ "Plant",
            grepl("plant_id", df$grp) ~ "Plant",
            df$grp == "year_fac" ~ "Year",
            df$grp == "date_fac" ~ "Date",
            df$grp == "Residual" ~ "Stigma",
            TRUE ~ "Other"
        )
        return(df[, c("Part", "level", "vcov", "sdcor", "percent")])
    }

    # Inter-Annual (Global)
    f_inter <- as.formula(paste(variable_col, "~ 1 + (1 | year_fac / plant_id)"))
    m_inter <- lmer(f_inter, data = data)
    res_inter <- extract_lmer_var(m_inter, "Inter-Annual")

    # Intra-Annual (2024 Only)
    data_24 <- filter(data, year == 2024)
    # Check if we have date variation in 2024
    if (length(unique(data_24$date_fac)) > 1) {
        f_intra <- as.formula(paste(variable_col, "~ 1 + (1 | date_fac / plant_id)"))
        m_intra <- lmer(f_intra, data = data_24)
        res_intra <- extract_lmer_var(m_intra, "Intra-Annual (2024 only)")
    } else {
        # Fallback if date is singular
        f_intra <- as.formula(paste(variable_col, "~ 1 + (1 | plant_id)"))
        m_intra <- lmer(f_intra, data = data_24)
        res_intra <- extract_lmer_var(m_intra, "Intra-Annual (2024 only)")
    }

    combined <- rbind(res_inter, res_intra)
    combined$Metric <- metric_label
    return(combined)
}

res_HP_supp <- run_twopart_vca_supp(vca_data_supp, "sqrt_HP", "Heterospecific pollen")
res_CP_supp <- run_twopart_vca_supp(vca_data_supp, "sqrt_CP", "Conspecific pollen")
all_results_supp <- rbind(res_HP_supp, res_CP_supp)
all_results_supp$level <- factor(all_results_supp$level, levels = c("Year", "Date", "Plant", "Stigma"))

# 3. Helper to format the GT table
make_vca_table <- function(data_subset) {
    table_detailed <- data_subset %>%
        select(Part, level, vcov, sdcor, percent) %>%
        rename(
            Analysis = Part,
            Source = level,
            Variance = vcov,
            Std_Dev = sdcor,
            Percent_Total = percent
        ) %>%
        mutate(
            Variance = round(Variance, 2),
            Std_Dev = round(Std_Dev, 2),
            Percent_Total = paste0(round(Percent_Total, 1), "%")
        ) %>%
        arrange(Analysis, desc(Source))

    last_inter_row <- max(which(table_detailed$Analysis == "Inter-Annual"))

    library(flextable)
    flextable(table_detailed) %>%
        set_header_labels(
            Analysis = "Analysis Scope",
            Source = "Variance Source",
            Variance = "Variance Component",
            Std_Dev = "SD",
            Percent_Total = "% Total"
        ) %>%
        hline(i = last_inter_row) %>%
        theme_vanilla() %>%
        set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1) %>%
        fontsize(size = 9, part = "all")
}

# Conspecific Pollen Table (First)
make_vca_table(filter(all_results_supp, Metric == "Conspecific pollen"))
```

# Section S4: Significance Testing of Variance Partitioning

To test the statistical significance of the variance components (Year, Date, and Plant) for both Heterospecific (HP) and Conspecific (CP) pollen deposition, we performed Likelihood Ratio Tests (LRT) using the `ranova()` function from the `lmerTest` package.

<br>

**Table S7: Significance Testing of Variance Components**  
*Likelihood Ratio Tests for Inter-Annual and Intra-Annual nested models.*

```{r}
#| label: table-s8-ranova
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(lmerTest)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# Prepare VCA data
vca_data <- pollen_deposition %>%
    filter(!is.na(heterospecific_pollen) & !is.na(conspecific_pollen)) %>%
    mutate(
        sqrt_HP = sqrt(heterospecific_pollen),
        sqrt_CP = sqrt(conspecific_pollen),
        year_fac = as.factor(year),
        date_fac = as.factor(paste(year, day, sep = "_")),
        plant_id = inflorescence_id
    )

# Inter-Annual Model Testing (Years 2022-2024)
m_inter_hp <- lmer(sqrt_HP ~ 1 + (1 | year_fac / plant_id), data = vca_data)
test_inter_hp <- ranova(m_inter_hp)
m_inter_cp <- lmer(sqrt_CP ~ 1 + (1 | year_fac / plant_id), data = vca_data)
test_inter_cp <- ranova(m_inter_cp)

# Intra-Annual Model Testing (2024 Only)
data_24 <- filter(vca_data, year == 2024)
m_intra_hp <- lmer(sqrt_HP ~ 1 + (1 | date_fac / plant_id), data = data_24)
test_intra_hp <- ranova(m_intra_hp)
m_intra_cp <- lmer(sqrt_CP ~ 1 + (1 | date_fac / plant_id), data = data_24)
test_intra_cp <- ranova(m_intra_cp)

# Formatting function
format_ranova <- function(ranova_res, model_type, pollen_type) {
    df <- as.data.frame(ranova_res)
    df$Term <- rownames(df)

    df <- df %>%
        filter(!is.na(LRT)) %>%
        mutate(
            Model = model_type,
            Pollen = pollen_type,
            Term = gsub("\\(1 \\\\| ", "", Term),
            Term = gsub("\\\\)", "", Term)
        ) %>%
        select(Model, Pollen, Term, npar, logLik, AIC, LRT, Df, `Pr(>Chisq)`)

    return(df)
}

res_list <- list(
    format_ranova(test_inter_hp, "Inter-Annual (2022-2024)", "Heterospecific"),
    format_ranova(test_inter_cp, "Inter-Annual (2022-2024)", "Conspecific"),
    format_ranova(test_intra_hp, "Intra-Annual (2024)", "Heterospecific"),
    format_ranova(test_intra_cp, "Intra-Annual (2024)", "Conspecific")
)

all_ranova <- do.call(rbind, res_list)

library(flextable)
flextable(all_ranova) %>%
    set_header_labels(
        Model = "Model Scope",
        Pollen = "Pollen Type",
        Term = "Random Effect",
        npar = "Parameters",
        logLik = "Log-Likelihood",
        AIC = "AIC",
        LRT = "LRT Statistic",
        Df = "df",
        `Pr(>Chisq)` = "P-value"
    ) %>%
    colformat_double(j = c("logLik", "AIC", "LRT"), digits = 2) %>%
    colformat_double(j = "Pr(>Chisq)", digits = 3) %>%
    theme_vanilla() %>%
    set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1) %>%
    fontsize(size = 9, part = "all")
```

# Section S4: Data Descriptions
## Overview
This document provides metadata, variable dictionaries, and summary statistics for the datasets associated with the manuscript. These datasets are archived for reproducibility and public access.

## Data Description
These datasets contain empirical data collected to investigate the mechanisms linking pollinator visitation networks to stigmatic pollen deposition on *Succisa pratensis*. The study investigates how community-level network structure (specialization, interaction evenness) and single-visit pollen deposition stochastics scale to population-level pollination outcomes across three years (2022-2024).

The provided files are:
- `pollen_deposition.csv`: Total pollen loads on stigmas collected from the field.
- `SVD.csv`: Single-visit deposition experimental data.
- `network_metrics.csv`: Aggregated yearly metrics constructed from three primary data sources: 
  1. **Plant-pollinator visitation networks**: Used to calculate network-level specialization ($H_2'$) and species-level specialization/interaction evenness for *Succisa pratensis* using the `bipartite` R package.
  2. **Stigmatic pollen deposition**: Used to calculate the linear slope of Conspecific (CP) vs. Heterospecific (HP) pollen accumulation, and mean HP loads.
  3. **Floral abundance transects**: Used to calculate the mean *Succisa pratensis* abundance per plot and total community floral abundance.
- `interaction_data_all_22_24.csv`: Full plant-pollinator visitation observation data for the entire community across all years.
- `interaction_data_Succisa_22_24.csv`: Subset of the visitation data containing only observations for *Succisa pratensis*.
- `plant_abundance_22_24.csv`: Floral abundance transect data for all plots across years.
- `pollen_load_and_guts_2024_Succisa_pratensis.csv`: Raw pollen load and gut content data for individual pollinators.

```{r setup-metadata, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(labelled)
```

df_svd <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "SVD.csv"))
df_network <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "network_metrics.csv"))

df_int_all <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "interaction_data_all_22_24.csv"))
df_int_succ <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "interaction_data_Succisa_22_24.csv"))
df_abund <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "plant_abundance_22_24.csv"))
df_pload <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "pollen_load_and_guts_2024_Succisa_pratensis.csv"))

## 1. Pollen Deposition Dataset (`pollen_deposition.csv`)
This dataset contains information regarding pollen deposition on individual stigmas of *Succisa pratensis* over three consecutive years.

### Data Dictionary
```{r dict-pollen}
var_label(df_pollen$id) <- "Unique sample identifier (Stigma ID)"
var_label(df_pollen$year) <- "Year of sampling (2022-2024)"
var_label(df_pollen$plant_id) <- "Unique plant/patch identifier"
var_label(df_pollen$conspecific_pollen) <- "Count of conspecific (Succisa) pollen grains on stigma"
var_label(df_pollen$heterospecific_pollen) <- "Count of heterospecific (non-Succisa) pollen grains on stigma"
var_label(df_pollen$pollen_total) <- "Total pollen count on stigma"

look_for(df_pollen, details = FALSE) %>%
  select(variable, label) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Variables in Pollen Deposition Dataset") %>%
  opt_stylize(style = 1, color = "blue")
```

### Summary Statistics
```{r summary-pollen}
df_pollen %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    N_Stigmas = n(),
    Unique_Plants = n_distinct(plant_id),
    Mean_CP = round(mean(conspecific_pollen, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    Mean_HP = round(mean(heterospecific_pollen, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  ) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Pollen Deposition Sample Sizes & Means") %>%
  opt_stylize(style = 1, color = "blue")
```

This dataset contains experimental observations of pollen deposition resulting from a single, uninterrupted visit by various pollinator morphogroups to virgin *Succisa pratensis* inflorescences.

var_label(df_svd$heterospecific_pollen) <- "Heterospecific pollen deposited during single visit"
